assertions.assert: On start, and on every later entry into `idle`, it offers nothing: it sends `bot.ability.offers` `{ability: "vocal", choices: []}` to its parent.

`bot.ability.vocal.speech.encoding.input` `{parts}` (1 to 64 parts `{expression?, words?}`) in `idle` is encoded by the speech service's `encode` with the `<param>`s `parts`, `model`, `voice`, `output` and `media_type` (`audio/pcm` by default); with provider `null` (the default) that is the OpenAI-compatible `POST {base}/audio/speech`. The service's answer is sent to the parent as `bot.ability.vocal.speech.encoding.output` `{audio, media_type, sample_rate_hz, channels, duration}` (the audio as the `output` reference; raw PCM is 24 kHz mono, its duration measured from its bytes; a format the service cannot measure has `null`s), and it returns to `idle`.

The `provider` `<param>` names the original's provider instead: `elevenlabs` is `POST {base}/text-to-speech/{voice}?output_format=…`, `gemini` is `POST {base}/interactions` (its answer's base64 audio part), each answered as above.

When the service answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message}` (an error status, an empty answer, an `output` that cannot be written), it sends the parent `bot.ability.failed` with the service's message and returns to `idle`.

When the service cannot run (a missing `voice`, rejecting its start with `error.execution`), it sends the parent `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "The speech service could not run (<error event>)."}` and returns to `idle`.
An input that arrives while `applying` is dropped: only the input in hand is encoded and answered.
Each input is a new encoding: after an answer or a failure, the next input in `idle` is encoded again.

The service says the parts as the original's encoders do: walking them in order, a part with a pause opens a new stretch, each stretch whose words are not blank is one backend request saying its words joined as written, one at a time in order, and no other cue (a sound, an emotion) is applied. With a pause the answers are joined as 16-bit PCM with each pause's silence at its place (0.4 s short, 1 s long), written raw for `audio/pcm` or in a WAV container for `audio/wav`; a pause with another `media_type` rejects the service's start, answered as in statement 5.
